items.headline: Wall Street is closed for the weekend after a mixed Friday and a strong week
items.note: On Friday, Nov. 13, the Dow rose 0.1% to about 52,348, while the S&P 500 fell 0.4% to about 7,562 and the Nasdaq fell 0.9% to about 25,136. All three still gained for the week, with the S&P up about 2.5%. Trading resumes Monday.

items.headline: Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday, days after CEO Jensen Huang resigned
items.note: An SEC filing says the board accepted Huang's resignation on Nov. 11 and named CFO Colette Kress interim CEO while it searches for a permanent one. The filing gives no reason. The stock fell more than 4% Friday and was down roughly 12% on the week, so Tuesday's report is the first big test.

items.headline: AMD, Broadcom and Intel also sold off Friday
items.note: AMD fell about 9%, Broadcom about 6% and Intel about 5%, so the weakness spread beyond Nvidia to the broader chip group. Chips are the heart of AI infrastructure, so this matters for AI-related hiring and valuations.

items.headline: Anthropic's IPO is expected to price this week, with trading on Nasdaq as ANT
items.note: Renaissance Capital lists 825 million shares at $70–$78, about $61 billion, plus a $26 billion private placement from investors including Google, Microsoft, Nvidia and AMD. Pricing is expected the week of Nov. 16. It would be the largest AI-lab listing so far.

items.headline: Traders bet on a Fed rate hike in December as the 10-year yield tops 5%
items.note: Producer prices rose 0.3% in October, below the 0.4% expected, but the 6.5% annual rate is the highest since November 2022. The 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.17%, its highest since October. The Fed meets Dec. 8–9; higher yields tend to weigh on tech stocks.

items.headline: The Fed held rates last month with two members voting to hike
items.note: A calendar summary says the FOMC kept the range at 3.75%–4.00% on Oct. 28 by a 10–2 vote, with the two dissenters favoring a hike. September CPI was 3.7% over 12 months. This is the background to the December rate-hike bets.

items.headline: Bitcoin slips below $70,000 and the VIX briefly tops 20
items.note: Bitcoin fell below $70,000 for the first time in nearly three months, and the VIX (a gauge of expected stock volatility) rose above 20 during Friday's session. Both point to nervous risk appetite as yields climb.

items.headline: Anthropic starts its IPO roadshow and adds Claude Meetings in beta
items.note: A newsletter digest (not an original source, which I didn't open) says Anthropic began its roadshow and is rolling out Claude Meetings to Team and Enterprise users, starting with Google Meet. It shows AI labs pushing into everyday workplace tools.

learn.explain: A bull market is a long stretch when stock prices are broadly rising, often defined loosely as an index climbing 20% or more from a low. A bear market is the opposite: prices fall 20% or more from a recent high, usually alongside gloomy sentiment. The names are just shorthand for the mood (bulls thrust horns up, bears swipe down). Real markets zigzag inside both. The week ended Nov. 6 saw the S&P 500 fall 2.7%, and the week after it gained about 2.5%, which is ordinary short-term noise rather than a new bull or bear market. A single bad week or day doesn't change which one you're in.
learn.try: Look up a chart of the S&P 500 over the last 10 years and mark the 20% drops from a peak to see where past bear markets happened.
